section.title: Lesson Narrative
section.para: In this lesson, students recall how to calculate the slope between two points when given two coordinates or a table, using the slope formula; or with a graph, using knowledge of rise over run. Students will then use this knowledge to write equations of lines in slope-intercept form, point-slope form, and standard form. Equations will be written from two points or one point and a slope. Students practiced finding slope from a graph in 1.10 but have not formally found the slope when given two coordinates or from a table. Also in 1.10, students explored writing and graphing equations using standard form. In 1.11.3, students had the opportunity to write equations from standard form to slope-intercept form by solving for \(y\) to identify \(m\) and \(b\). They will still need practice converting equations into all three different, equivalent forms.
section.title: Learning Goals (Teacher Facing)

list.item: Write the slope of a line given two points from coordinates, a table, or a graph.
Write equations in slope-intercept form, standard form, and point-slope form.
Write equations given two points or one point and the slope of a line.

section.title: Learning Targets (Student Facing)

list.item: Write the slope of a line.
Write the equation of a line in different forms.
